sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:37

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:37:1
items.html: It returned and turned its face downward toward Bina and gave the seven lights: For the matter of the departure of the light from the vessel of Hochma is what causes the turning of its face downward, which is the aspect of equivalence with the face of Bina; for it annulled its former face, that is, its phase two, and made its posterior, that is, phase one, into the aspect of face. And so it is now face to face with Bina, and therefore it can bestow to her the level of phase one, which is the level of ZA, now called after its highest Sefira, which is the light of Hesed, and which includes all seven lower Sefirot: HGT NHYM. And this is what he says, and it turned its face downward toward Bina and gave her the seven lights. And there are now in Bina eight lights, which are the remainder of the light of the male that she received from Hochma, which is phase two, as above, and a further seven lower ones that are included in phase one, which she now received from the female of Hochma; thus eight lights.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:37:2
items.html: Every giving of lights is always in the aspect of face to face. As was explained above, the bestower and the receiver must be in equivalence of form with one another. Therefore, as long as its face is upward, it is much higher than the receiver, and they do not touch one another, and therefore it does not bestow — unless it annuls its face and sets its posterior as face; and then the faces of the bestower and of the receiver are found to be equal to one another, which is called face to face. And for the explanation of the matter, see well in the Inner Light above, page 305, the passage beginning “and then the vessel.”
